auditlens.reply:
Yes
Verifiable from git: confirming the remote head against the local commit and verifying commits with git log ensures that claimed states match actual repository history. This closes the loophole where pipe exit masking or hook failures allowed phantom progress to be reported. While push output files and five-minute refusal reporting happen in the workspace rather than git history, comparing remote and local refs anchors verification in objective git state. Note: the file-based exit logging should eventually be captured in card verification records so external audits can inspect push outcomes directly from repo artifacts.
CITE: every push writes its whole output and its own exit code to a file
